picks.headline: Oklahoma Sooners vs. Texas Longhorns final score predictions: Red River Rivalry could see a familiar trend
picks.blurb: Oklahoma Sooners vs. Texas Longhorns final score predictions: Red River Rivalry could see a familiar trend - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Mike Ditka dies at 86 Valkyries finish sweep Buccaneers stun Cowboys Worker to Dak: 'Embarrassing' NFL injury tracker updates Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 8, 2026 at 4:46 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oklahoma Sooners will take on the Texas Longhorns in the Red River Rivalry, and it could be closer than some think. The Oklahoma Sooners and Texas Longhorns have one of the biggest rivalries in sports. The Red River Rivalry is truly a spectacle . But the last few years haven't been as much of a game as we, as sports fans, have hoped for. This one could be the same way. Texas is the No. 1 team in the country. Oklahoma is no longer ranked, and shouldn't be. But Texas seems beatable despite being No. 1 overall. They could have lost to Tennessee not long ago. Yet the Sooners, with their baggage, still have a chance this weekend. However, not many are picking them to win. Final score predictions for Oklahoma vs. Texas Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame: Texas 21, Oklahoma 10 This feels like an ugly, low-scoring battle for much of the afternoon, with both defenses dictating the pace. Oklahoma's defense presents a major challenge for Texas, forcing Arch Manning to make a couple of crucial plays in difficult situations. Manning doesn't need to put up huge numbers, but he delivers when the Longhorns need him most and does just enough to keep the offense moving. Oklahoma's bigger issue is its offense, which struggles to sustain drives against a talented Texas defense. The Sooners find a few opportunities but can't capitalize enough to keep pace. Texas eventually creates some separation late, with Manning making the key throws to secure a hard-fought 21-10 victory in a game that never feels particularly comfortable for either side. Craig Smith , A to Z Tennessee: Texas 26 Oklahoma 9 I've watched Oklahoma a number of times this season, and I haven't seen many Power Four offenses worse than the Sooners' this year. I also haven't seen many defenses better than the Longhorns' this year. Colin Simmons is one of college football's most dominant defenders, totaling 5.5 sacks against Tennessee in one of the best overall defensive performances we've seen from a player and a team this season. Now, a floundering OU offense with no answers for getting John Mateer and the passing attack going will have to find a spark against one of the country's best defenses. I don't expect it will go any better than it did for the Sooners against Georgia. OU gives Texas some short fields, and that's all the Horns need to take control. Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida: Texas 19, Oklahoma 7 We've seen some wild things in Red River, and this game likely won't be an exception. The one thing that stands out is Oklahoma's offense. I don't trust what John Mateer is going to be able to do. He's gone from a fun quarterback at Wazzu to a player with a broken brain. I don't think Mateer will do much against the Longhorns, but I can see the defense getting the Sooners on the board because that unit can flat-out play. Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama: Texas 27, Oklahoma 19 Typically, Red River is one of the more anticipated games on the college football schedule, but that doesn't seem to be the case this year. That has little to do with Texas, however, as the No. 1-ranked Longhorns have held up their end of the hype deal; it has everything to do with Oklahoma, OU's offense, and John Mateer. The year-two leap at Oklahoma hasn't come to fruition, and Mateer may have regressed from how he looked pre-thumb injury to his current state. But I don't think it's all on Mateer. Oklahoma just doesn't have easy buttons on offense outside of Isaiah Stategna, and Ben Arbuckle hasn't exactly inspired much confidence with his scheme. I don't see a world where OU can score enough to keep up with the Longhorns. Justin Churchill , A to Z Oklahoma: Texas 19, Oklahoma 13 The Oklahoma Sooners are in a bad spot right now. As we write this, they're dismissing their freshman wide receivers. But in other news, the offense is broken. And there's really no fixing it. However, the defense is still good enough to win them games. They just need decent play from the offense from time to time. I still don't think that happens this week. They're not healthy. Meanwhile, Texas looks good, especially on defense. Their offense can be efficient but has its own issues. This one is going to go to the Longhorns once again. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Thomas Jones Thu, October 8, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Over the past four seasons, Texas football has seized control of the Red River Rivalry series against bitter rival Oklahoma . The No. 1 Longhorns (4-0, 1-0 SEC) have won three of the past four games for the first time since 2006-09, and they've limited Oklahoma (2-2, 0-1) to a total of nine points in those three victories. This video created with the assistance of AI. Based on the betting lines, that dominance should continue Saturday for Texas. For just the second time in the game's 126-year history, the Longhorns enter the game atop the Associated Press poll while the Sooners arrive unranked. Texas beat then-No. 1 Ohio State and picked up a hard-fought SEC road win two weeks ago at Tennessee. The Sooners have struggled so far with unimpressive wins over UTEP and New Mexico as well as losses at Michigan and Georgia. But a triumph in the Cotton Bowl could change the course of the season and take some heat off head coach Brent Venables, who's tallied a 34-22 record since taking over the OU program in 2022. Here's a full scouting report for the Texas Longhorns vs. the Oklahoma Sooners: MORE: Texas vs OU predictions: How many points for Arch Manning; how many Colin Simmons sacks? No. 1 Texas (4-0, 1-0 SEC) vs. Oklahoma (2-2, 0-1) When: 2:30 p.m. Saturday Where: Cotton Bowl in Dallas TV/radio: ABC, 1300, 98.1, 105.3 (Spanish) Weather: The State Fair should enjoy sunny skies and almost ideal weather, but it could get warm in the sun. Temperatures should climb into the high 80s, but a nice breeze will keep things from getting too sticky . Texas vs Oklahoma football betting info Moneyline: Texas -330, Oklahoma +260 Spread: Texas is favored by 7½ points. Over/under : 39½ Texas history: Oklahoma All-time: Texas leads 65-51-5 Last meeting: Texas 23, Oklahoma 6 (Jan. 1, 1969) Most memorable meeting: Texas 26, Oklahoma 20 (1968). Texas won in a stirring comeback behind quarterback James Street in just his second game as the Longhorns ' starter. The second straight win for a Texas team that had tied and lost in the first two weeks of the season kicked off the most dominant stretch in school history, which included a 30-game win streak and back-to-back national titles in 1969 and 1970. File photo of the Texas vs. Notre Dame Cotton Bowl game that took place January 1970. Pictured center is #16 quarterback, James Street with Coach Darrell Royal. (The Dolph Briscoe Center for American History, The University of Texas at Austin) Know the foe: Oklahoma Last game: Lost at Georgia, 41-13 (Sept. 26) Players to watch: QB John Mateer , a 6-foot-1, 225-pound senior from the Dallas suburb of Little Elm, has struggled in his fifth and final collegiate season. He's thrown for 883 yards, eight touchdowns and four interceptions and has just 76 yards rushing after picking up 1,255 yards and 23 touchdowns on the ground over the previous two seasons. WR Parker Livingstone , a 6-3, 200-pound junior, spent his first two years at Texas and even roomed with Longhorns QB Arch Manning. Livingstone transferred to Oklahoma during the offseason and has drawn some good-natured ribbing from Manning and Texas coach Steve Sarkisian, but he's had minimal impact for the Sooners with six catches through four games as well as a costly fumble against Michigan. Texas Longhorns receiver Parker Livingstone (13) makes a catch during the game against Florida at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 4, 2025 in Gainesville, Florida. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) DL David Stone, a 6-3, 315-pound junior, dislocated a kneecap in practice last month but returned in time for the Georgia game. He has just 14 tackles and two stops for a loss this season but remains one of the SEC's elite run defenders. Central Texas connections: WR Isaiah Sategna III, who leads OU with 20 catches for 267 yards, graduated from Fayetteville (Ark.) High School but has Austin ties. His father, Mario Sategna, once coached track and field for Texas and the younger Sategna once played on a Pop Warner football team in Westlake with former UT safety Michael Taaffe and current New York Jets QB Cade Klubnick. … DT Jacob Henry , an Austin native who played at Lake Travis and Vandegrift, attends OU on a wrestling scholarship but also plays for the football team. He's the son of Mark Henry, a noted Texas booster and former professional wrestling star who co-hosts a popular radio show in Austin with Mike Hardge. When Texas has the ball Sarkisian has become cagey about injuries , deferring to the ambiguous injury reports that teams release each day beginning Wednesdays of game week. But RB Hollywood Smothers should return this week after missing the Tennessee game, and his explosiveness will help against OU, which has struggled against the run. Smothers averages 4.8 yards a carry, which leads all Texas players who have at least 10 carries, Oklahoma ranks just 42nd in the nation by allowing 115.5 yards per game on the ground. The Sooners are stingy in the red zone; they've given up points on just 60% of opponents' drives into the red area, which tops all Power Four programs. Senior safety Peyton Bowen and younger brother Eli, a cornerback, lead a veteran secondary that could cause problems for Manning and his receiving corps. The Sooners rank fourth in the nation by allowing 122.5 yards per game while Texas ranks just 71st with 231.3 yards passing. But the Oklahoma DBs aren't exactly ballhawks; they have just one interception. Six decades after Duke Carlisle paved the way, Texas' Arch Manning set for Dallas When Oklahoma has the ball Can Oklahoma block a Texas pass rush led by Colin Simmons, who had a single-game school record 5½ sacks against Tennessee two weeks ago? OU's struggling offensive line ranks just 120th in the nation as a unit in Pro Football Focus's pass blocking grades, and the Longhorns rank fourth in the SEC with 15 sacks. If Mateer can't get protection, the Sooners may not reach the end zone for a fourth time in the past five games. The offensive line's struggles extend to the ground game. The Sooners average only 2.9 yards per carry, while the offense ranks last in the SEC in total offense with 321.3 yards per game. That doesn't bode well against a Texas defense that leads the SEC in scoring defense (13.3 ppg) and is fourth in total defense (271.0 ypg). Linebacker Rasheem Biles (30 tackles) and safety Jelani McDonald (26 tackles) both boast sideline-to-sideline range. Texas vs Oklahoma key matchup Texas DE Lance Jackson vs. Oklahoma RT E'Marion Harris Simmons will unquestionably get added attention from the Oklahoma pass protection after his record-setting performance against Tennessee. That means Jackson, a 6-5, 275-pound sophomore, could get lots of one-on-one chances against E'Marion Harris opposite Simmons. Texas vs Oklahoma prediction Thomas Jones: Texas 26, Oklahoma 9. The Sooners are scrappy on defense, especially in the red zone. But their beleaguered offense will have problems crossing midfield against what may be the best defense in the SEC. Danny Davis: Texas. Bad Texas teams have beaten good Oklahoma teams and vice versa, but that won't happen this weekend. Oklahoma will actually score a touchdown this year, but Sooners fans will be in line for Corny Dogs by the middle of the fourth quarter. Cedric Golden: Texas 31, Oklahoma 17. The Oklahoma defense is no joke, but it will be the second best defense in Dallas, including the Cowboys. Colin Simmons comes up with two more sacks and Arch and Co. will do enough to pull this one out. Answer: Who's on your Mount Rushmore of college football? While the panel of top scribes from San Antonio, Houston, Austin and Dallas came to no consensus, it is clear that the Sooners enter the game with a host of worries against a Texas team ranked No. 1. So, how does our group of experts see the 122nd edition of the Red River Rivalry? Kevin Sherrington Only twice has a No. 1 team ever lost in this rivalry, and both times it was Oklahoma, in 2008 and 1963. I don't see Texas making it three. Arch Manning hasn't exactly lit it up, but the Sooner Schooner is a wreck. Only Brent Venables' defense can keep it from being a blowout. Texas 24, Oklahoma 13 Shawn McFarland Brent Venables spoiled the X-factor of this week's game when he criticized the development of his offensive line. Against Texas' Colin Simmons and Co., with a weak offensive line and with a quarterback who struggles under pressure, this year's installment will mirror the last two. It might even be the worst of the three. Texas 31, Oklahoma 3 Lia Assimakopoulos These games are usually closer than expected, even when there's as large of a divide between the teams as it appears Texas and Oklahoma have this year. But the No. 1 Longhorns have already proved themselves against tough opponents like Ohio State and Tennessee, while the John Mateer-led Sooners have struggled against not only Georgia and Michigan, but even underwhelmed against New Mexico. Texas should take this one easily. Texas 24, Oklahoma 10 Oklahoma has had a week off to try and get things straight after being throttled by No. 2 Georgia in a turnover-filled mess. And the 'Dawgs don't have the pass rush that Texas does. John Mateer has had a rough enough start; can you imagine how bad things may go if Colin Simmons is constantly breathing down his neck? Texas 31, Oklahoma 13 The Sooners have failed to score a touchdown in three out of the last four Red River clashes. With the Oklahoma offense struggling, John Mateer spiraling and the Texas defense surging — not to mention the absence of Lewisville's Michael Fasusi, the anchor of the Sooners' O-line — they'll have just as much trouble finding the end zone on Saturday. Texas 27, Oklahoma 9 While anything can happen in a rivalry game, the No. 1 Longhorns should take care of Oklahoma (2–2) for the third straight year after winning at the Cotton Bowl 23-6 last season and 34-3 in 2024. Texas has already survived two tight games against tough competition — a 24-23 home win over Ohio State in Week 2 and a 20-17 road victory over Tennessee in late September — and junior edge Colin Simmons is playing like a first-round draft pick. The Duncanville product posted a Texas program-record 5.5 sacks during the win in Knoxville on Sept. 26 and made 2.5 against the Sooners last year. But Oklahoma won't make it easy on the Longhorns, as the Sooners try to bounce back from a 41-13 loss to Georgia in Week 4. The National Council on Problem Gambling help line is also often cited at 1-800-522-4700. Broadcast Details - TV: ABC and ESPN Unlimited (Sean McDonough, Greg McElroy and Katie George) - Radio: Sooner Sports Network via 107.7 The Franchise/KOKC 95.3 and 1520 in Oklahoma City, 1430 The Buzz/KMOD 97.5 in Tulsa, and on The Varsity Network app (Toby Rowland, Teddy Lehman, Chris Plank, and Gabe Ikard) - National Radio: Compass Radio (Bill Jones and Tiki Barber) What You Need To Know DALLAS - The setting is familiar. The circumstances are not. Oklahoma and Texas meet for the 98th straight year Saturday at 2:30 p.m. CT at the Cotton Bowl, and the Sooners listed as the designated home team. That is where the comfort ends. Texas is 4-0, ranked No. 1 in both major polls, and playing like the standard in the sport right now. Oklahoma is 2-2, unranked for the first time all season, and coming off a month that left more questions than answers. This is the Red River Rivalry with the roles flipped hard. The Sooners are not walking into Dallas as the hunted. They are walking in as the side that has to prove it still belongs in the same sentence. The degree of difficulty is historic enough on its own. Oklahoma just faced No. 2 Georgia . Now it gets No. 1 Texas . That makes this only the fourth time the Sooners have played the AP's top two teams in back-to-back games, joining 1963, 1987, and 2000. It is also just the fourth time since 2000 that any FBS team has drawn No. 1 and No. 2 in consecutive regular-season games. That is not a soft rivalry week. That is a measuring stick with no place to hide. The ranking split adds another layer. Since 2013, when one of these teams has been ranked and the other has not, the unranked side is 4-3. Oklahoma itself is only 3-4 against Texas since 1971 when entering the game unranked. Those numbers keep the door cracked open just enough to create hope. They do not change the larger truth. Texas is better right now, and Oklahoma has to play a near-perfect game to make this feel like a fight for four quarters. That starts on defense, because it has to. The Sooners still have a unit good enough to keep them alive. Oklahoma leads the nation by allowing just one passing touchdown and ranks among the national leaders in red-zone defense, first downs allowed, third-down defense, passing defense, and total defense. The identity is still there. The front can disrupt. The back end has been stingy. Every defensive starter through four games began his college career at Oklahoma , which matters in a rivalry game that usually rewards toughness and continuity more than portal gloss. The problem is that defense is going to be asked to cover for an offense that has not returned the favor. Oklahoma is averaging 22 points and barely more than 320 yards a game. The run game has been a mess. The offensive line has been inconsistent. John Mateer has had enough productive moments to stay in the conversation and enough damaging ones to keep the temperature high. He enters the week with 883 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and a 66.1 percent completion rate. That is fine on paper. The turnovers and stalled drives are why nobody in Norman feels fine about it. Across the field is Arch Manning , and that matchup alone would be enough to make this week heavy. Manning has 862 passing yards, seven touchdowns, and three interceptions for a 4-0 Texas team that does not need the game script to get exotic to beat you. He can throw with velocity, process quickly, and hurt a defense with his legs if contain breaks down. Brent Venables already called him a player with no real weaknesses in the talent package. Oklahoma's best chance is not to eliminate him. It is to make him uncomfortable with interior pressure, late coverage disguise, and a physical perimeter. There are a few offensive crumbs the Sooners can point to. Mateer has already hit six touchdown passes of 20-plus yards this season. The tight end room has been more useful than expected under Jason Witten, especially Rocky Beers, who has 18 catches for 255 yards and has given Mateer a reliable intermediate option. Isaiah Sategna III remains the one receiver who can still change a drive by himself. That is not a complete offense. It is a group that has to become efficient enough to keep the defense from living in an impossible game script. Recent history does not help Oklahoma's nerves either. Last year's Red River game followed a familiar painful pattern: the Sooners hung around into halftime, then disappeared after it in a 23-6 loss. Texas controlled the third quarter, converted third downs, and turned a one-score game into a statement. Oklahoma had 12 tackles for loss that day and still could not get off the field often enough. That is the danger again this week. Play well in stretches and still lose the game in the moments that decide it.The larger backdrop is Year 3 in the SEC for both programs, and the contrast is getting harder to ignore. Texas looks like a national title contender. Oklahoma looks like a team still searching for offensive stability after a 10-win playoff season a year ago. The schedule has been brutal again, and it is not about to ease up after Dallas. But none of the remaining résumé talk matters if the Sooners cannot find a way to stay competitive against the top team in the country in the rivalry that still defines so much of the brand. Oklahoma's defense is good enough to give the game a pulse. Texas is complete enough to take it away in a hurry if the Sooners' offense stays stuck in the same place. Red River does not care about bye-week quotes, rankings debates, or how respectable the defensive profile looks on paper. It cares about which team imposes itself when the stadium is split down the middle and every possession feels louder than the last. Oklahoma needs clean football, a functional line, and a low-event afternoon from Manning. Texas needs to be itself. That is why this one feels so heavy.

away.headline: Oklahoma Sooners' injury report for matchup vs. Texas Longhorns opened eyes to an issue that's been going on since 2024
away.blurb: The Oklahoma Sooners head into the Red River Rivalry against the Texas Longhorns with a long injury list. At this point, what's new? Banged-up rosters have become the norm for OU over the last few years. Ever since the SEC's player availability reports started in 2024, the Sooners have almost always carried a health disadvantage into game day. George Stoia of SoonersScoop.com pointed out a number that puts it in perspective, and I think it's worth mentioning. Stoia laid it out: OU averages 10.25 players on the initial availability report since it began in 2024. Its opponents averaged 6.68. OU has had fewer players on the initial report only once-the College Football Playoff game against Alabama. The Sooners had 6 players on that report. That feels about right. Nobody needs to stat-check it, either. Thursday's availability report for OU vs. Texas tells the same story . The Sooners have five players listed as out, two doubtful, one questionable, and five probable. Oklahoma – Out: Taylor Heim, Trell Harris, Xavier Robinson, Jacobe Johnson, Fred Hinton – Doubtful: Trynae Washington, Michael Fasusi – Questionable: Eddie Pierre-Louis – Probable: Jer'Michael Carter, Cole Sullivan, Michael Boganowski, Owen Heinecke, Jack Van Dorselaer. Texas – Out: Kaliq Lockett, Jordan Coleman, Zion Williams – Questionable: Justus Terry That's 13 names for Oklahoma and four for Texas. That's just how it is for the Sooners every week. When the Wednesday report came out, some fans were legitimately concerned. The list looked worse than it did heading into the Georgia game, even though OU had a bye week in between. More names showed up after a week off, not fewer. So fans scrambled to figure out how a team gets more injured during a bye. Fair enough, that's a decent question to ask. How does that work? I have no idea. Most likely, some players got more banged up in the Georgia game, and we just didn't know about it going into the bye. That's why building depth in the NIL era matters so much. You're going to have injuries, and OU seems to have more than anybody. Maybe that perception is right, maybe it's wrong. Regardless, the depth has to be better. You can sit here and look at this issue all you want and try to figure out what's going wrong internally. The game still has to be played. Texas isn't going to skip the Red River Rivalry because Oklahoma has a lot of guys on the report. You'd love to see the Sooners keep building their depth so the next man up can carry more of the load. For now, the Longhorns definitely have the advantage. Texas is already the No. 1-ranked team in the country, and the Sooners are coming in with really bad football. With 13 players on the availability report, OU will need its backups to step up. Texas gives injury non-update on Hollywood Smothers, Nick Townsend status once again Skip to main content Recruiting After nearly a week and a half since we last saw the Texas Longhorns take the field against the Tennessee Volunteers, many people were eager to hear how previously injured players had progressed over the bye. However, what should come as no surprise is that Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian had another idea in mind : no update. With star players like running back Hollywood Smothers, tight end Nick Townsend, and defensive lineman Justus Terry all missing time this season, Longhorn Nation has been eager to see their guys back in action. Unfortunately, we will have to wait to see what we should expect on Saturday. "I think we're healthier than we were a week ago at this time," Sarkisian said in his game preview press conference, continuing his refusal to share injury updates beyond what he puts in the SEC-mandated availability reports. Steve Sarkisian sticks to SEC availability report and nothing more On Monday of Week 4, before the Horns faced the Vols, Sarkisian expressed a similar sentiment, refusing to update members of the media on any lingering injuries, stating that "There's called an injury report in the SEC, so that's enough of the injury questions," Sarkisian said that week. Based on the final injury list from Texas's game against Tennessee, one could easily assume that Smothers will be good to go against the Oklahoma Sooners this weekend as the Horns prepare for the annual Red River Rivalry. The star running back was off the report just before kickoff and was seen on the sidelines in full pads, with his helmet on, but never entered the game against the Volunteers. However, when it comes to Terry and Townsend, your guess is as good as mine. Smothers is nursing a reported lower-leg injury suffered in practice, Townsend is healing up from a knee injury he sustained before Week 2's kickoff, Terry is recovering from a toe injury ahead of Week 2's game, Coleman hasn't played since Week 3, and Filsaime has yet to take the field this season. For right now, Texas fans (and Oklahoma fans) will have to wait to see what Texas's injury list looks like on Wednesday evening, because until then, Sarkisian is remaining tight-lipped about the health of his team. home.headline: Oklahoma Sooners' injury report for matchup vs. Texas Longhorns opened eyes to an issue that's been going on since 2024
home.blurb: The Oklahoma Sooners head into the Red River Rivalry against the Texas Longhorns with a long injury list. At this point, what's new? Banged-up rosters have become the norm for OU over the last few years. Ever since the SEC's player availability reports started in 2024, the Sooners have almost always carried a health disadvantage into game day. George Stoia of SoonersScoop.com pointed out a number that puts it in perspective, and I think it's worth mentioning. Stoia laid it out: OU averages 10.25 players on the initial availability report since it began in 2024. Its opponents averaged 6.68. OU has had fewer players on the initial report only once-the College Football Playoff game against Alabama. The Sooners had 6 players on that report. That feels about right. Nobody needs to stat-check it, either. Thursday's availability report for OU vs. Texas tells the same story . The Sooners have five players listed as out, two doubtful, one questionable, and five probable. Oklahoma – Out: Taylor Heim, Trell Harris, Xavier Robinson, Jacobe Johnson, Fred Hinton – Doubtful: Trynae Washington, Michael Fasusi – Questionable: Eddie Pierre-Louis – Probable: Jer'Michael Carter, Cole Sullivan, Michael Boganowski, Owen Heinecke, Jack Van Dorselaer. Texas – Out: Kaliq Lockett, Jordan Coleman, Zion Williams – Questionable: Justus Terry That's 13 names for Oklahoma and four for Texas. That's just how it is for the Sooners every week. When the Wednesday report came out, some fans were legitimately concerned. The list looked worse than it did heading into the Georgia game, even though OU had a bye week in between. More names showed up after a week off, not fewer. So fans scrambled to figure out how a team gets more injured during a bye. Fair enough, that's a decent question to ask. How does that work? I have no idea. Most likely, some players got more banged up in the Georgia game, and we just didn't know about it going into the bye. That's why building depth in the NIL era matters so much. You're going to have injuries, and OU seems to have more than anybody. Maybe that perception is right, maybe it's wrong. Regardless, the depth has to be better. You can sit here and look at this issue all you want and try to figure out what's going wrong internally. The game still has to be played. Texas isn't going to skip the Red River Rivalry because Oklahoma has a lot of guys on the report. You'd love to see the Sooners keep building their depth so the next man up can carry more of the load. For now, the Longhorns definitely have the advantage. Texas is already the No. 1-ranked team in the country, and the Sooners are coming in with really bad football. With 13 players on the availability report, OU will need its backups to step up. UCLA also averages 10 penalties per game, which McElroy said ranks 137th out of 138 teams, and that number becomes harder to overcome in a road environment like Autzen. History favors the Ducks, too. In 2022, the Bruins started the season 6-0 before going to Oregon, but that UCLA team was a bit of a mirage. No, this isn't at the 1998 level yet, when the team was 10-0 and deep in the national title hunt before losing in a historic 49-45 thriller against Edgerrin James and Miami. And no, this UCLA team isn't there yet in Bob Chesney's first season, but if it pulls this off, everything changes. Oregon got back to being Oregon again with a 41-27 win over USC, but Dante Moore is out, Dylan Raiola is in, and this is when it has to flex at home and show just how much the Week 2 loss to Oklahoma State was a blip. UCLA vs Oregon: Quick Hits Oregon gets three home games in the next four weeks. It plays unbeaten UCLA this week, hosts currently unbeaten Nebraska next week, goes to Illinois, and then hosts Northwestern before traveling to Ohio State. UCLA plays three home games in a row after this, hosting Wisconsin, Michigan State, and Nevada before going to Minnesota. Oregon has won five straight in the series since 2017, last winning 34-13 in 2024. away.headline: Oregon Ducks Injury Report Delivers Dante Moore News Before UCLA
away.blurb: Coming out of a bye week with extra time to rest and recover, fans waited for the first injury report for the No. 13 Oregon Ducks’ matchup against the No. 21 UCLA Bruins with perhaps more anticipation than usual. Below are the players listed as out, doubtful, questionable and probable. The Big Ten requires each program to update its availability beginning three days ahead of the game. Oregon’s next injury report is expected at 5 pm. PT on Thursday. While fans will have to wait a little longer to see him in action, Moore’s teammates expressed the boost in morale the team gained from seeing him in practice. Lanning addressed having him out there during his Wednesday press conference. “Yeah, I think the biggest thing is just being able to see a smile on his face to get around and be around his teammates and his brothers and do that at a high level, which is fun,” Lanning said. “Everybody has a smile on their face getting to see Dante out there with us this week, and it's been fun seeing him compete.” “He had an expectation when he stepped out there on the field and performed at a really high level, and everybody had confidence in him because they see him do it a lot in practice,” Lanning said. “You get a lot of reps in practice, regardless of where you're sitting.” As soon as Moore announced in the offseason that he’d forgo the 2026 NFL Draft and return to Oregon, the outside expectation from many was that the transfer Raiola would back up Moore and become a regular starter in 2027. But with Moore’s injury and slow build-up to his return to play keeping him out against the Bruins, Saturday could mark Raiola’s starting debut at Oregon. Ducks linebacker Jerry Mixon expressed on Tuesday that Raiola’s prior experience and his preparation give the team confidence in him. “He's been ready the whole time, learning from Dante,” Mixon said. “Yeah, he's been starting for two years, so he knows what to do when he get out there.” Dante Moore’s Injury Return Gets a Cautious Outlook From Pete Thamel Quarterback Dante Moore’s second-quarter exit against the No. 19 USC Trojans with a scary hit that resulted in a concussion raised questions about his availability. Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB The LSU Tigers will hit the road this weekend to face the Kentucky Wildcats to kick off seven straight SEC games left in the season. Another road game for the Tigers could mean some simialr struggles they faced in Ole Miss, the one loss of the season so far. But luckily, this isn't Kiffin's highly anticipated return to his former program. The trip to Lexington will bring its own challenges, ones that LSU can handle. Both teams enter the SEC matchup with a 4-1 record, each with one SEC loss. Kentucky has some serious momentum after the past three weeks of straight wins, with two major upsets over conference opponents. The Wildcats shut down the Texas A&M Aggies at Kyle Field in a 31-21 win, before upsetting the South Carolina Gamecocks last weekend, also on the road, in a 35-34 overtime win. That win marked the largest road comeback in program history. LSU also dominated Texas A&M, with a 35-6 win in Week 4 and an at-home 63-14 win against McNeese State last weekend. Now, Kentucky ranks 3rd in the SEC, while LSU sits at No. 7. Still, the Wildcats will need this mid-season momentum if they want a chance over the Tigers. While Kentucky has had an impressive run so far this year, the Tigers have the chance to shut it down on Saturday, claiming the first on-the-road win of the season over the Wildcats. The roster matchup points to LSU as a clear winner, with Kentucky having obvious weak spots that the Tigers can dominate in. Kentucky QB Kenny Minchey has already been sacked 11 times this year, which is guaranteed to be a problem against LSU's defense. LSU defensive end Princwill Umanmielen now leads the conference in sacks with eight this season. That's going to pose a major threat to Minchey. There's also a hidden weapon on the Tigers' offense, with transfer running back Dilin Jones dominating this season with 426 rushing yards and five touchdowns. So far, Kentucky's defense has allowed 144 rushing yards per game, being a weak spot that Jones can win over for scoring production and moving the drive downfield. Meanwhile, LSU's defense has held opponents to 58 rushing yards per game, creating a major challenge for Kentucky's running back CJ Baxter, who has put up 361 rushing yards this season. It's a matchup that favors LSU on paper, which will continue into Saturday Night's game in Lexington. The Tigers get the road win over a quality opponent. Loading recommendations... picks.headline: Kentucky vs #10 LSU: Final Thoughts and Prediction
picks.blurb: Kentucky vs #10 LSU: Final Thoughts and Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Mike Ditka dies at 86 Valkyries finish sweep Buccaneers stun Cowboys Worker to Dak: 'Embarrassing' NFL injury tracker updates Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky vs #10 LSU: Final Thoughts and Prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Fri, October 9, 2026 at 5:27 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football hosts the No. 10 LSU Tigers in the first night game of the season on Saturday, and the atmosphere at Kroger Field will be one of the best of all time. We have previewed Lane Kiffin's offense and Blake Baker's defense, as the Tigers have high level talent all over the field. We also laid out Kentucky's path to victory in this football game. It will take the Wildcats best shot to take down the Tigers, here are my final thoughts and prediction. A lot of people are overlooking LSU's side of the injury report as they are without two All-American level players in tight end Trey'Dez Green and linebacker Whit Weeks, the Tigers will also be without starting nickel Dashawn Spears. Kentucky is down linebacker depth in a big way, as Alex Afari, Tavion Wallace and Antwan Smith are all out for this game. Kentucky is also down their backup nickel Jaden Smith, but the starting nickel Aaron Gates returns after missing last week. Kentucky is at full strength offensively, running back Jason Patterson and wide receiver DJ Miller are both ready to go. We have talked all week about the crossover between these two teams; the long relationship between Kentucky offensive coordinator Joe Sloan and LSU defensive coordinator Blake Baker. Louisiana product and breakout true freshman Kenny Darby was committed to LSU at one time. Kentucky has multiple players that were at LSU at one point in their career: left tackle Lance Heard, wide receiver Nic Anderson and defensive tackle Ahmad Breaux. There is one crossover we have not mentioned this week... LSU has a familiar face leading their offensive line, that is coach Eric Wolford. Coach Wolford could not revive the big blue wall during his two stints in Lexington. LSU has a lot of talent on the offensive line, left tackle Jordan Seaton is one of the top NFL Draft prospects at his position. However, that unit has had some rough outings this season (shocking) and the interior offensive line is gettable; Kentucky's defensive line has to win the line of scrimmage and get pressure on quarterback Sam Leavitt. Another area of the game we have yet to mention is how good Kentucky has been in the "middle 8", these are the last four minutes of the first half and the first four minutes of the second half. Kentucky leads the country in points per drive on offense in the middle 8 and this has to continue in this game. The defense for the Wildcats have performed much better in the middle 8 as well. You can look at the graph of full FBS teams below, this is something to watch closely on Saturday. Kentucky just has to play their style of football to win this game, granted they have to do it almost flawlessly to come away with a massive victory. Kentucky has to win the turnover margin, which is something they have consistently done this season. The defense has been very opportunistic and the Wildcats have done a phenomenal job at staying on schedule offensively. Kentucky can utilize their unique offensive scheme to move the football and score points, but the Wildcats have to create explosives on this Blake Baker defense that allows explosives. Kentucky has done really well on a few areas defensively. The Wildcats rank 6th in the SEC in EPA per dropback allowed and explosive play rate allowed. Kentucky also ranks 2nd in the conference in turnover forced percentage. If Kentucky can limit explosives for the Tigers and create explosives on offense, they will be in a great position to win this football game. It is worth noting that Kentucky is 5-0 against the spread in their last five meetings against top ten teams, and they have won three of those games outright as underdogs. LSU is not at full strength, down both players that had the honor of wearing the legendary number 7 in the Tigers program. Kentucky is closer to full strength as the starting 22 is healthy and ready to go for this one. This is a game that I originally predicted a loss for the Wildcats, but I think Kentucky has a ton of momentum right now and will benefit from an incredible atmosphere at Kroger Field. Prediction: Kentucky 31, LSU 28 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky vs #10 LSU: Final Thoughts and Prediction

The LSU Tigers will look to avoid a "letdown" this weekend in a road matchup against the Kentucky Wildcats. Saturday will mark the first matchup between the two programs since 2021 when Kentucky beat LSU 42-21 in Lexington. ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of LSU vs Kentucky ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Alabama quarterback, made his predictions on Tuesday for this weekend's biggest games, and he has LSU just barely getting by Kentucky. "I'm taking the LSU Tigers to win the game 30-24," said McElroy . "I think they're going to win this game with the pass rush, and I do think there's going to be plenty of opportunities for LSU's defensive front to create some advantages behind the line of scrimmage. "But with (LSU QB) Sam Leavitt still a little bit limited right now, I think this one has a chance to stay pretty close for a really long time. Kentucky's comeback last week (against South Carolina) was historic, but against this pass rush, they can't afford to be playing from behind from start to finish." It's never easy to win on the road in the SEC. Kentucky isn't as daunting of a venue as some other places in the conference, but it can still be a challenge. LSU would love to win this game by multiple touchdowns, and maybe they do, but just simply getting the win is the top objective for the Tigers on Saturday night in Lexington. The last time that LSU played in Lexington, it didn't go very well for the Tigers. LSU lost 41-21 on the road to Kentucky in 2021. It was the second straight SEC loss for the Tigers under then head coach Ed Orgeron. It was a loss that all but sealed the fate of Orgeron (especially after he admitted that LSU's defensive line got out-physicaled). The Tigers will return to Lexington this weekend for a matchup against the Wildcats. And while no players remain on the roster from the 2021 LSU team, I'm sure head coach Lane Kiffin will use the loss to Kentucky in 2021 as motivation. ESPN's Cole Cubelic shares how he thinks the LSU vs Kentucky game will play out ESPN's Cole Cubelic shared some thoughts this week on the LSU vs Kentucky matchup. Cubelic noted that he likes the momentum that Kentucky has right now, but he doesn't think the Wildcats can consistently pressure Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt. "I like this game being at Kroger Field," said Cubelic . "I like the momentum Kentucky has right now. The problem is that Kentucky can't get to the quarterback, and I think Sam Leavitt has gotten better in the pocket — he was forced to (get better in the pocket) with the hamstring two weeks ago against Texas A&M. And he did it again last week. "[Leavitt] being able to find success from the pocket and Kentucky not being able to get home, that's going to be a problem. And LSU is going to score. So I think LSU gets the win. I'm not going to touch the 8.5 (points) there that LSU is favored by, but I may like the over 51.5 in this game." LSU and Kentucky will kick off at 6:00 PM CT/7:00 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ESPN. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. Lane Kiffin's Tigers are 4-1, just about where we expected them to be at this point. LSU's lineup looks a little different than it did in Week 1. Injuries, along with typical early-season shuffling, have adjusted the Tigers' depth chart, especially on offense. Let's take a look at LSU football's updated offensive depth chart through five weeks. No surprises at quarterback. Sam Leavitt remains LSU's QB1. He earned the job in the spring and hasn't looked back. Down the depth chart, though, the lineup isn't as consistent. Stacy Gage was LSU's RB2 to start the season, but that role belongs to Harlem Berry now, who rose from RB4 in recent weeks. Eugene Wilson, Jackson Harris, and Winston Watkins have emerged as LSU's top-three wide receivers, though Watkins is coming off a rough game where he dropped two touchdowns. Jayce Brown and Tre Brown both produced at their previous stops, but haven't seen much action with the first-team in recent weeks. away.headline: Thursday’s LSU vs. Kentucky injury report
away.blurb: The second injury report of the week is out and there are no changes for the Tigers. There was a little movement for the Wildcats, though. LSU was able to stay healthy through the McNeese game last week and that shows on this report. The latest of anyone listed as OUT to have gotten hurt was Whit Weeks against Texas A&M two weeks ago. The six players listed as out remained the same from Wednesday, but there were a few other changes. DL Kalen Edwards was downgraded from questionable to doubtful. home.blurb: The LSU Tigers return to SEC play this weekend against the Kentucky Wildcats, which means another week of official injury reports to prepare for the week. While the first couple of weeks of reports brought chaos and some disappointing news, this is a pretty chill week for the Tigers (less so for the Wildcats). Here are the initial reports put out by the conference : No news is good news for LSU. They have five players ruled out, but all were expected to be out. There was nothing unexpected here. It is good to see the cornerback depth improving, with Ja'Keem Jackson off the report entirely. It is a long list for Kentucky this week, but nothing completely detrimental. They do have five players already listed out, the same as the Tigers, but only one was a Week 1 starter. Their depth has been completely wiped out, which could always come into play as well. LB Antwan Smith LB Alex Afari Jr. LB Tavion Wallace DB Jaden Smith DB Grant Grayton RB Jordan Colbert LS Cole Marszalek DL Kalen Edwards The best news for the Wildcats comes in the fact that running back Jason Patterson and defensive back Aaron Gates are not on the report. That's an important role against this Lane Kiffin offense. picks.headline: Bold Predictions for Georgia-Alabama Showdown
picks.blurb: Bold Predictions for Georgia-Alabama Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Alabama Crimson Tide and the Georgia Bulldogs will face off on Saturday and are going to have to weather both the storm of each other and Hurricane Isaias. As always, this matchup brings memorable moments. It brings drama. It brings instant-classics. I have to find a way to get bold with it. I lost out on all three of my bold predictions for the Vanderbilt game after hitting on one against Oklahoma. Fortunately, I have seen this movie plenty of times. Here are three bold takes for the game between Kirby Smart’s Dawgs and Kalen DeBoer’s Crimson Tide that I think can legitimately happen. 5 Total Turnovers Between Both Teams The ground will be wet, the wind will be hard and the rain will be coming down. The weather is projected to calm down for actual gametime, but now tabbed as Hurricane Isaias is going to make its mark all the way up the state of Alabama. You know what that means: sloppy football. We already saw the Georgia Bulldogs struggle with fumbles during the rainy Western Kentucky game in the second week. I suspect that could be an issue again if the weather truly is complicated. Alabama’s quarterback Keelon Russell, as good as he is, has not faced a defensive unit as talented or as violent as Georgia’s. He has been pretty clean this year, throwing only two interceptions and losing only one fumble to this point, but I predict he turns the ball over at least once himself. I would probably predict that even without the weather. Turnovers happen when these two teams face off. The weather will induce more of them. I am predicting five will come true. Gunner Stockton Scores Two Touchdowns on the Ground Georgia’s redshirt senior quarterback has yet to score a touchdown with his legs this season – something he did 10 times in 2025, leading the Dawgs in that category. I think he will do it twice on Saturday night. Stockton has not carried the ball near as much this season as he did at this point a year ago. He exploded for almost 100 yards on the ground at Arkansas thanks to a career-long 62-yard run. Georgia also hasn’t played in a big game yet. Stockton’s legs were a favorite in their important matchups a season ago. The danger comes in the red zone for opposing defenses. He had a red zone rushing touchdown against Tennessee. He ran two in against Kentucky. He scored the dagger with his legs against both Texas and Auburn. He ran one in from 22 yards out against Ole Miss in the regular season and then ran for two scores against the Rebels in the Sugar Bowl. I think Stockton will find the end zone again, and I think it will happen twice. It is the piece of Georgia’s red zone offense - which is extremely multiple - that hasn’t been dished out yet this season. Nate Frazier has his first 100-Yard Game of the Season Especially because of the potentially awful weather, I think Georgia is going to run the football a ton. Nate Frazier has gotten his rest since getting dinged up against Arkansas. He was off to a super hot start that has been slowed down due to him virtually missing 2.5 games. Chauncey Bowens has been ruled out for this game due to a foot injury he suffered last weekend. Even with the emergence and explosiveness of Dwight Phillips Jr., Frazier will likely see the bulk of the touches out of the backfield. Georgia is fresh off a smackdown on Vanderbilt, 38-14, while Alabama dismantled Mississippi State 56-23. This has game of the year potential, and there's been a lot of them in the SEC already! Georgia has the No. 1 rated offense and defense per PFF, averages the most points in the country, and allow the third-fewest rushing yards per game (57.4) — and all of that will be put to the test against Alabama. The Bulldogs pitched a second-half shutout against Vanderbilt and won 38-14 after leading 21-14 at the half. Georgia has allowed 20 or fewer points in all five games and 44 points over the last three games against Arkansas, Oklahoma, and Vanderbilt. The offense put up 471 total yards of offense, doubled Vanderbilt's first downs (26-13), and held the Commodores to 85 rushing yards. Alabama is coming off arguably their most impressive performance of the season. The Tide destroyed Mississippi State, 56-23, never trailing in the game. Alabama outgained Mississippi State in yards 483-302, went 6-of-9 on third downs, and forced four turnovers (2 INT, 2 Fumbles). Keelon Russell had another dominant outing with 301 total yards and four touchdowns (3 pass, 1 rush). Russell is climbing the Heisman Trophy rankings and a win over Georgia would likely jolt him to the top spot. Alabama has owned the series against Georgia winning 10 of the past 12, but the Bulldogs won the previous matchup 28-7. Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Game Details and How to Watch Georgia vs Alabama Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026 Time: 7:30 PM Eastern Site: Bryant-Denny Stadium City: Tuscaloosa, AL TV/Streaming: ABC Game Odds for Georgia vs Alabama The latest odds as of Tuesday courtesy of DraftKings : Moneyline: Georgia Bulldogs (+102), Alabama Crimson Tide (-122) Spread: Alabama -1.5 (-112) Total: 52.5 points #2 Georgia Bulldogs Head Coach: Kirby Smart 2026 Record: 5-0 (3-0) Offensive Points Per Game: 51.4 PPG (1st) Defensive Points Per Game: 13.4 (12th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 97th 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 20th The Georgia Bulldogs Offense: Georgia is the highest scoring offense in the country which is odd because in years past, Kirby Smart has taken is foot off the gas against early season opponents. Georgia's scored 45, 41, and 38 points against SEC opponents so far with 471, 464, and 306 total yards of offense. Georgia ranks sixth in third-down offense (54.9%), fifth in passing efficiency (188.72), and 13th in turnover margin per game (+1.2). One area that will be of interest is Georgia's red zone offense is 51st in the country with a 25-of-28 conversion rate (89.3%), but the fourth-most red zone attempts. Georgia has to be aggressive in the red zone at Alabama. Field goals likely won't cut it. Georgia Player to Watch on Offense: QB Gunner Stockton In last year's SEC Championship Game, Gunner Stockton threw for three touchdowns on 20-of-26 for 156 yards. Georgia cruised 28-7. This matchup won't be as easy and could feature double the points. Stockton tossed three touchdowns versus Vanderbilt last week after combing for two touchdowns in the two weeks prior. Stockton hasn't been asked to do much this season due to all the talent around him, including the running back committee. Stockton has a 13:1 TD to INT ratio this season and a 75.7 completion percentage. The Georgia Bulldogs Defense: Georgia's allowing 244.6 yards per game (7th) and that will likely go up after this showdown. We know Georgia is great at getting pressure (PFF rank of 22 for pressure) or getting coverage sacks (PFF rank of 3 for coverage), but the two areas that will determine the game is third downs and red zone defense. Georgia's defense has a 33.8% third-down defense (44th) and have only allowed 11 red zone trips this season, but 10 of them have resulted in points (8 TDs, 2 FGs). Georgia Player to Watch on Defense: LB Chris Cole Chris Cole is a projected first round pick in the upcoming draft as a three-year player for Georgia. Cole opened the season with a half-sack, and added anther against Oklahoma with two fumble recoveries. Cole had 60 tackles last season, ranking fourth, and a team-leading 4.5 sacks. Cole has 22 tackles and 1.5 sacks to this season. Last year, Cole had five tackles versus Alabama and a sack. Alabama Player to Watch on Offense: QB Keelon Russell Keelon Russell now has a rushing touchdown in three-straight games and four out five, plus three or more passing touchdowns in three consecutive games. He is on fire and now the third in odds for the Heisman. Russell now has 11 passing touchdowns to two interceptions, 1,414 yards through the air, and 184 on the ground. Russell had his fewest pass attempts (22) on the season against Mississippi State but was efficient with a 72.7 completion percentage, 285 passing yards, and four total touchdowns. Georgia will be his toughest test yet, but if this is a shootout and Alabama wins, then Russell will be the favorite for the Heisman and Bama could climb as high as No. 1 or 2 in the AP Poll. The Alabama Crimson Defense: The Alabama defense may be flying under the radar this year because of how well the offense has been playing. The Tide allow 78.6 rushing yards per game (10th) due to teams falling behind and abandoning the run, rank 15th in third-down defense (27.5%), and have the seventh-best turnover margin per game (+1.4). One of the negatives has been the red zone defense, which ranks 117th with a 92.9% conversion rate — 13 out of 14 red zone opportunities have resulted in points for Alabama's opponents. That will be something to watch in this top 10 showdown. Alabama Player to Watch on Defense: DL Devan Thompkins Devan Thompkins is projected tone a first round pick and will likely be in the middle of some big third down stops. Thompson opened the year with three combined sacks, a forced fumble and recovery against Kentucky and Florida State. In the last two games, Thompkins has 1.5 TFL and no sacks, but impacted plenty of plays as a 6-foot-5 300-pounder. Georgia ranks 13th and 4th in pass and run blocking per PFF, let's see how Thompkins feels about that. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 19 USC desperately needs a win to remain in the CFP hunt, while Penn State looks to avoid a 0-3 start in the Big Ten Imagn Images It's a must-have for both teams , as No. 19 USC hits the road to take on Penn State Saturday night in Happy Valley. Penn State enters the game with its season seemingly spiraling out of control. After a 3-0 start in nonconference play under new coach Matt Campbell, the Nittany Lions have dropped their first two Big Ten games, and didn't look particularly inspiring in either. The offense struggled mightily in losses to Wisconsin and Northwestern , and last week, the defense was gashed by Northwestern's rushing attack. Suddenly, a schedule that was considered one of the easiest in the Big Ten before the season began looks far more difficult for the Nittany Lions. Not that things have been much easier for their opponents. The Trojans are 5-1 on the season and are coming off a win, but have looked shaky for three straight games. They found themselves in a shootout with Rutgers three weeks ago, followed that up with a 14-point home loss to Oregon , and last week flirted with disaster against a Washington team that hadn't looked impressive to start the season. Now they're on the road against a team with its back against the wall, and a second loss (with Ohio State and Indiana still to come) could crush USC's playoff chances. USC vs. Penn State: Need to know It's the White-Out game: Penn State's White-Out game is a newer tradition in college football , having begun in 2007, but it's quickly become one of the games Penn State fans look forward to most. Everybody in Beaver Stadium is dressed in white and screaming at their absolute loudest. Unfortunately, the results haven't always matched the intensity. Penn State is only 11-7 in White-Out games, but that's partly because the Nittany Lions reserve the tradition for their toughest games. It's a battle of the two winningest QBs in college football: That fact probably caught you by surprise, didn't it? Well, it's true. Penn State's Rocco Becht comes into this game with 29 wins as a starting QB in his college career. That's more than any other QB in the country. USC's Jayden Maiava is tied for second with 24. So Becht will either widen the gap this week, or Maiava will narrow it. Penn State hoping to avoid a 0-3 start in Big Ten again: Last season, the Nittany Lions started 0-6 in Big Ten play. It was an unexpected slide that led to James Franklin's mid-season firing. If they lose here, they'll be 0-3 in the Big Ten for the second straight season. The last time that happened was the 2003 and 2004 seasons. Of course, Matt Campbell could take some solace if his team loses. Students walking around the campus heard lots of crowd noise coming from the Trojans practice field. That's because USC blared that energy through the loud speakers. Even true freshman edge rusher Luke Wafle admitted to being spooked by the sound. "It scared me the first time they were doing sound checks, and I was walking out of my class," Wafle told reporters on Oct. 8. The Saturday, Oct. 10 matchup marks the seventh time the former Oklahoma coach, Riley, will face the ex-Iowa State leader, Campbell. But it'll be the first time they meet in the Big Ten. Riley owns the upper hand in the head-to-head matchups against Campbell's Cyclone teams, going 4-2 all-time against him and ISU. But Riley already knows what to expect from a Campbell-led team . "Going back to Iowa State, they've always used their tight ends really well, and they're doing so here [Penn State]. Defensively, they look a lot like the past Penn State teams in being big up front," Riley said during his Oct. 5 appearance on Trojans Live. "They've got really good athletes and talented players, and they're excellent on the back end. It's a well-coached football team, and it'll be a heck of a night." Oregon blocked out the noise and won in double overtime to prevent a Penn State home win. And the Ducks turned to a silent count on offense to withstand the noise. Perhaps USC rolls with something similar in this showdown. But Riley's past success against Campbell, plus USC showing signs of resurgence on defense, should be enough to avoid the upset. Penn State hosts USC on Saturday night as the Trojans make their first visit to Beaver Stadium since 1994 and for the first time as a Big Ten opponent. The Trojans bring a dangerous offense to the game but are faced with some concerns about the defense. Can Penn State find its offense against the Trojans and pull off a big win against a ranked opponent in the whiteout game? The Trojans enter this weekend following a 25-21 comeback victory over Washington, while the Nittany Lions have lost consecutive Big Ten games. Both teams are desperate to change the narrative this weekend. Who actually can? 1. USC's Passing Attack Faces Its Biggest Road Test NCAA Football: Fresno State at Southern California Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Jayden Maiava is central to USC's chances. The quarterback averages 311.7 passing yards per game and has shown he's able to sustain drives, converting 52.1 percent of the offense's third-down attempts. Penn State's pass defense, however, is a major counterweight to USC's offensive firepower. They have playmakers in the secondary, including Audavion Collins, who entered the matchup tied for fourth nationally with seven pass breakups. If Penn State consistently disrupts Maiava's timing, the Trojans could struggle to maintain their usual offensive rhythm. 2. Penn State's Run Game Must Respond Penn State's most pressing problem is its rushing defense. It allowed 413 rushing yards in a 34-13 loss to Northwestern, a collapse that exposed tackling problems and difficulty controlling the line of scrimmage. And it's especially concerning against a USC offense capable of exploiting defensive gaps. Rocco Becht must also protect the football. He threw interceptions in consecutive losses, including a multi-interception performance against Northwestern. Penn State needs more sustained drives, better protection, and a more effective ground attack to prevent USC from dictating the tempo. 3. Penn State has a 6-1 record in its previous seven White Out games before losing to Oregon in double overtime last season. The environment gives the Nittany Lions a legitimate chance to turn their season around. But USC has shown some resilience, rallying past Washington with 15 unanswered points, and has been efficient on third and fourth downs, which could help them neutralize the crowd by extending possessions. USC's injury situation bears watching, particularly the availability of receiver Trent Mosley, who has missed time recently. The betting market has reflected the uncertainty, with Penn State a short home favorite despite USC's stronger record. That makes this a particularly interesting test of whether the Nittany Lions can correct their defensive problems quickly enough. USC vs. Penn State Prediction: Who Wins? Maiava should find enough opportunities downfield, while the Trojans' offense can control possession and force the Nittany Lions to keep pace. away.blurb: Washington suffered a neck injury during spring practice and was due to be re-evaluated last week. Fisch said on Monday that it looks like the Huskies will not get the third-year runner back in action for a long while, however, so it's probably safe to assume that Washington is out for the season. Moss will not be re-evaluated until November 1 after suffering a soft-tissue injury on the first play of the Washington State game. Chris Lawson has started three games in his absence at the X receiver position and is second on the team in receiving with 13 catches for 212 yards and a touchdown. Fisch said this week that their understanding is that Moss, a sixth-year senior, will be out of eligibility due to the NCAA eliminating injury waivers with the advent of 5-in-5 eligibility beginning this season. Carr will also not be re-evaluated until November 1 after suffering a hand injury against Washington State that required surgery. He had 5 carries for 28 yards before the injury, which opened the door for Limar to lead the Huskies backfield in the second half. With Carr, Limar, and Washington all out, freshman Brian Bonner Jr. and sixth-year Trey Cooley will continue to split reps in the Huskies backfield. Christian tore his Achilles during spring practice and is out for the season. He has remained around the team, but like Moss, will likely be out of eligibility after the year even with the injury wiping out his season. Hatchett suited up against Minnesota but was ruled out on the gameday report, but Fisch said that he would be a game-time decision this week.
